text: Europe focusEurope’s strategic buildout: the Netherlands in focusSeptember 2026 | Strategic strengths and supply constraints are shaping investment needs across security, energy and technology — and competitive returns will determine where capital flows.Read the full report (PDF)Europe’s investment challenge has sharpened since our 2025 paper as powerful mega forces increasingly converge. Geopolitical fragmentation has raised the value of resilience and made defense a more structural priority, while the AI buildout increasingly depends on power and physical infrastructure. In a world shaped by supply constraints, Europe needs to expand capacity across three connected areas: security, energy and technology.The Netherlands sits at the intersection of these three strategic areas. Semiconductor equipment maker ASML and the wider Dutch high-tech ecosystem give Europe globally important capabilities, alongside strengths in security and logistics. At the same time, grid congestion and the closure of the Groningen gas field make the physical constraints on expansion clearly visible. That combination makes the Netherlands a useful case study of whether strategic strengths can scale as bottlenecks are eased.Europe’s import dependencyNet energy imports as a share of energy use, 1990-2023Source: BlackRock Investment Institute, with data from the World Bank and International Energy Agency, August 2026. Note: The lines show net energy imports as a share of total final energy consumption by country.The Dutch policy response is becoming more concrete. The government-commissioned Wennink agenda, pension reform and plans for a National Investment Institution are putting greater emphasis on implementation and capital allocation. That matters because while Europe has large pools of savings, not enough is being channeled into the equity and growth financing needed to expand capacity. But even if more risk-bearing capital becomes available, it will flow first to projects and companies that can scale and deliver competitive returns.Europe’s macro backdrop remains challenging. That keeps us selective. Higher public spending can lift activity, but the investment case depends on whether that spending creates capacity that can lift productivity, earnings and returns. We see nearer-term opportunities in defense technology, cyber, grids and electrical equipment, power and infrastructure financing. Over longer horizons, the opportunity set could broaden to semiconductors, AI infrastructure, automation, advanced manufacturing, energy systems and climate-resilient infrastructure if Europe can execute on reforms and expand capacity.Roelof SalomonsChief Investment Strategist for the Netherlands and the Nordics – BlackRock Investment InstituteRoelof is Chief Investment Strategist, Northern Europe at BlackRock, advising on macro, markets and portfolios.Chris KaminkerHead of Sustainable Research & Analytics - BlackRock Investment InstituteWei LiGlobal Chief Investment Strategist, BlackRock Investment InstituteJean BoivinHead of BlackRock Investment Institute
